name: Claude Code
tagline: API key, Claude subscription, or the installation AI proxy
description: Anthropic's terminal coding agent. SAM starts it in your workspace, streams its work into project chat, and can run many sessions side by side, each in its own workspace.
seoTitle: Run Claude Code on Your Own Cloud | SAM
seoDescription: Run Claude Code agents on cloud VMs you control with SAM, the open-source agent platform. Use an Anthropic API key, a Claude Pro or Max subscription, or an Anthropic-compatible endpoint.

features.title: Three ways to pay
features.description: Your Anthropic API key, your Claude Pro or Max subscription (guided sign-in, no terminal), or the installation's AI proxy if your SAM administrator turns it on.

features.title: Anthropic-compatible endpoints
features.description: Point Claude Code at another Anthropic-compatible API, for example a gateway your company already runs.

features.title: Several accounts
features.description: Connect a work subscription and a client's API key side by side, then pin each to the projects or profiles that should use it.

features.title: Pull requests when you ask
features.description: The agent works on its own branch and pushes it when the task is done. Ask, and it opens a pull request.

howItWorks.description: In Settings → Agents, sign in with your Claude subscription or paste an API key.
Choose Claude Code and a model in an agent profile, or use the project default.
SAM places the work on a machine, builds your devcontainer and starts Claude Code.
Follow along in project chat, steer it while it works, and review the branch or pull request.

useCases.title: Parallel feature work
useCases.description: Split a project into tasks and run one agent per task, each in its own workspace and branch.

useCases.title: Large refactors
useCases.description: Describe the pattern once and let several sessions work through different parts of the codebase.

useCases.title: Scheduled and event-driven work
useCases.description: Run Claude Code from a schedule, a GitHub event or a webhook using a saved profile.

faq.question: Which models can I choose?
faq.answer: The Claude 5 models, including Claude Fable 5.2, Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5 and Haiku 5.5, plus the Claude 4 models. Choose one in an agent profile.

faq.question: Do I need an Anthropic API key?
faq.answer: No. You can sign in with a Claude Pro or Max subscription instead, or use the installation AI proxy if your administrator has enabled it.

faq.question: Where does Claude Code run?
faq.answer: On a cloud VM, inside your repository's devcontainer, using a cloud account connected to your SAM installation. A profile can choose an Instant session on Cloudflare Containers instead, which needs no cloud account but does not use your devcontainer.

name: OpenAI Codex
tagline: API key, ChatGPT subscription, or the installation AI proxy
description: OpenAI's coding agent, run on your own machines instead of OpenAI's sandbox. SAM installs it in your workspace, keeps its sign-in fresh across parallel sessions, and limits it to the tools your project gives it.
seoTitle: Run OpenAI Codex on Your Own Cloud | SAM
seoDescription: Run OpenAI Codex agents on cloud VMs you control with SAM, the open-source agent platform. Use an OpenAI API key, a ChatGPT subscription, or an OpenAI-compatible endpoint.

features.title: Three ways to pay
features.description: Your OpenAI API key, your ChatGPT subscription (guided sign-in with a one-time code), or the installation's AI proxy if your administrator turns it on.

features.title: Safe token refresh
features.description: SAM serializes ChatGPT token refresh per user, so parallel Codex sessions do not invalidate each other's sign-in.

features.title: Only the tools you give it
features.description: SAM turns off Codex's built-in apps and plugins, so a session has only the tools and skills from SAM, your project and your profile.

features.title: OpenAI-compatible endpoints
features.description: Point Codex at another OpenAI-compatible API through a custom base URL.

howItWorks.description: In Settings → Agents, sign in with ChatGPT or paste an OpenAI API key.
Choose Codex and a model in an agent profile.
SAM places the work on a machine, builds your devcontainer and starts Codex.
Follow along in project chat and review the branch or pull request.

useCases.title: Bug triage in parallel
useCases.description: Turn several bug reports into tasks and let one Codex session investigate each.

useCases.title: Migrations
useCases.description: Framework upgrades, dependency bumps and language version changes, split across sessions.

useCases.title: Second opinion
useCases.description: Run Codex and Claude Code on the same task with different profiles and compare the branches.

faq.question: Do I need a ChatGPT subscription?
faq.answer: No. You can use an OpenAI API key, a ChatGPT subscription, or the installation AI proxy if your administrator has enabled it.

faq.question: Which models can I choose?
faq.answer: GPT-6 Astra, GPT-6.1 Sol, GPT-6.1 Terra, GPT-6 Sol, GPT-6 Luna and the GPT-5.6 models. A few older models work only with an API key.

faq.question: Where does Codex run?
faq.answer: On a cloud VM, inside your repository's devcontainer, using a cloud account connected to your SAM installation. A profile can choose an Instant session on Cloudflare Containers instead, which needs no cloud account but does not use your devcontainer.

name: Gemini CLI
tagline: Google's terminal agent with a Gemini API key
description: Google's open-source command-line coding agent. Add a Gemini API key and SAM runs it in your workspace with Gemini 4 and Gemini 3 models.
seoTitle: Run Gemini CLI on Your Own Cloud | SAM
seoDescription: Run Google Gemini CLI agents on cloud VMs you control with SAM, the open-source agent platform. Bring a Gemini API key and choose Gemini 4 or Gemini 3 models.

features.title: Gemini 4 and Gemini 3
features.description: Choose Gemini 4 Argon, Gemini 3.8 Flash, Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview or a lighter Flash-Lite model per profile.

features.title: API key sign-in
features.description: Add a key from Google AI Studio. SAM injects it into the workspace when the agent starts.

features.title: Your toolchain
features.description: Gemini CLI runs inside your repository's devcontainer with the same runtimes and test tools your team uses.

howItWorks.description: Paste a Gemini API key in Settings → Agents.
Choose Gemini CLI and a model in an agent profile.
SAM places the work on a machine and starts Gemini CLI in your devcontainer.

useCases.title: Cost-sensitive batches
useCases.description: Use Flash or Flash-Lite models for many small tasks, such as adding types or fixing lint.

useCases.title: Comparing agents
useCases.description: Run the same task with Gemini CLI and another agent and compare the results.

faq.question: Which models can I choose?
faq.answer: Gemini 4 Argon and the Gemini 3 models, such as Gemini 3.8 Flash and Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview. Gemini 2.5 remains for existing users until Google retires it.

faq.question: Can I sign in with a Google account instead of a key?
faq.answer: Not yet. SAM signs Gemini CLI in with a Gemini API key.

faq.question: Where does Gemini CLI run?
faq.answer: On a cloud VM, inside your repository's devcontainer, using a cloud account connected to your SAM installation. A profile can choose an Instant session on Cloudflare Containers instead, which needs no cloud account but does not use your devcontainer.

name: Google Antigravity
tagline: Google's Antigravity agent with Gemini models
description: Google's agentic coding tool. SAM downloads the pinned release on first use, checks its SHA-256 digest, signs it in with your Gemini API key and runs it in your workspace or an Instant session.
seoTitle: Run Google Antigravity on Your Own Cloud | SAM
seoDescription: Run Google Antigravity coding agents on cloud VMs you control, or in Instant sessions, with SAM. SAM installs a pinned, digest-checked release and signs it in with your Gemini API key.

features.title: Gemini models
features.description: Choose Gemini 3.8 Flash, Gemini 3.5 Flash, Gemini 3.1 Pro or another Gemini model Antigravity offers.

features.title: Verified install
features.description: SAM downloads the pinned release from Google on first use and checks its SHA-256 digest before running it.

features.title: Permission modes
features.description: SAM's permission modes map to Antigravity's own, so Bypass Permissions runs unattended and Manual asks before acting.

howItWorks.description: Paste a Gemini API key under Google Antigravity in Settings → Agents.
Choose Google Antigravity and a Gemini model in an agent profile.
SAM installs Antigravity on first use and runs your task. The first start downloads about 320 MB.

useCases.title: Trying Google's agent on real repositories
useCases.description: Compare Antigravity with Gemini CLI, Claude Code or Codex on the same project without installing anything locally.

useCases.title: Gemini work in parallel
useCases.description: Run several Antigravity sessions at once, each in its own workspace.

faq.question: Which models are available?
faq.answer: Gemini models only. Antigravity offers its Claude and GPT models only to clients Google recognizes by name, and SAM is not one of them yet.

faq.question: Can I send a message while it is working?
faq.answer: Yes. Antigravity cannot take a message into a running turn, so SAM delivers it as the next message when the turn ends.

faq.question: Does it work on every devcontainer?
faq.answer: It needs Linux x86_64 or arm64 with glibc. Alpine (musl) images are not supported.

name: Mistral Vibe
tagline: Mistral's coding agent with a Mistral API key
description: Mistral AI's command-line coding agent. Add a Mistral API key and SAM runs Vibe in your workspace with Mistral Large 3 by default, or Codestral, Mistral Small 4 and the Ministral models.
seoTitle: Run Mistral Vibe on Your Own Cloud | SAM
seoDescription: Run Mistral Vibe coding agents on cloud VMs you control with SAM, the open-source agent platform. Bring a Mistral API key and choose Mistral Large 3, Codestral or Ministral models.

features.title: Mistral models
features.description: Mistral Large 3 by default, Codestral for code-focused work, Mistral Small 4, and Ministral 3 in 14B, 8B and 3B sizes. Z.ai GLM 5.3 is also listed.

features.title: API key sign-in
features.description: Add a key from the Mistral Console. SAM injects it into the workspace when the agent starts.

features.title: Installed with uv
features.description: SAM installs Vibe with uv, the Python package manager. uv fetches the Python 3.12 it needs itself.

howItWorks.description: Paste a Mistral API key in Settings → Agents.
Choose Mistral Vibe and a model in an agent profile.
SAM places the work on a machine and starts Vibe in your devcontainer.

useCases.title: European model provider
useCases.description: Pair Mistral models with an EU cloud such as Hetzner, Scaleway or Infomaniak. The SAM control plane itself runs on Cloudflare's global network.

useCases.title: Small, frequent tasks
useCases.description: Use Ministral or Mistral Small for many cheap tasks and Mistral Large for harder ones.

faq.question: Which models can I choose?
faq.answer: Mistral Large 3, Mistral Small 4, Codestral, Ministral 3 (14B, 8B and 3B) and Z.ai GLM 5.3. Mistral Medium 3.5 is listed as deprecated.

faq.question: Does everything stay in the EU?
faq.answer: Model calls go to Mistral and machines run in the cloud region you choose. Chat history is stored in the Cloudflare account that runs your SAM installation, which is a global network.

faq.question: Where does Vibe run?
faq.answer: On a cloud VM, inside your repository's devcontainer, using a cloud account connected to your SAM installation. A profile can choose an Instant session on Cloudflare Containers instead, which needs no cloud account but does not use your devcontainer.

name: OpenCode
tagline: OpenCode Zen, OpenCode Go, or any OpenAI-compatible endpoint
description: SST's open-source coding agent. SAM installs a pinned, digest-checked build and runs it against OpenCode Zen, OpenCode Go, or an OpenAI-compatible endpoint you supply, such as a model server you host yourself.
seoTitle: Run OpenCode on Your Own Cloud | SAM
seoDescription: Run OpenCode agents on cloud VMs you control with SAM. Use OpenCode Zen, OpenCode Go, or any OpenAI-compatible endpoint, including one you host yourself.

features.title: Three inference options
features.description: OpenCode Zen (the default), OpenCode Go, or a custom OpenAI-compatible endpoint with your own base URL and key.

features.title: Live model lists
features.description: SAM loads the Zen and Go model lists from Models.dev, with a built-in list if that catalog is unavailable.

features.title: Open source end to end
features.description: OpenCode is open source, and so is SAM. Your security team can read both.

features.title: Pinned, verified build
features.description: SAM installs a specific OpenCode release with a SHA-256 check, on glibc and musl images.

howItWorks.description: In Settings → Agents, pick OpenCode Zen, OpenCode Go, or Custom and enter its key (and base URL for Custom).
Choose OpenCode and a model in an agent profile.
SAM places the work on a machine and starts OpenCode in your devcontainer.

useCases.title: Self-hosted models
useCases.description: Point the custom provider at a model server your machines can reach for a setup where prompts never reach a model vendor.

useCases.title: Trying open models
useCases.description: Switch between models on OpenCode Zen and Go without changing your workflow.

faq.question: Which inference providers can I use?
faq.answer: OpenCode Zen, OpenCode Go, and any OpenAI-compatible endpoint. Zen and Go use an OpenCode API key.

faq.question: Is OpenCode the same as OpenAI Codex?
faq.answer: No. OpenCode is a separate open-source project from SST.

faq.question: Can I use my own fine-tuned model?
faq.answer: Yes, if it is served behind an OpenAI-compatible API. Choose Custom and enter the base URL.

name: Amp
tagline: Amp's managed coding agent with an Amp API key
description: Amp is a coding agent that picks its own models and bills through Amp credits. Add an Amp API key and SAM runs it in your workspace like any other agent.
seoTitle: Run Amp on Your Own Cloud | SAM
seoDescription: Run Amp coding agents on cloud VMs you control with SAM, the open-source agent platform. Bring an Amp API key; SAM provisions the machine and manages the session.

features.title: Managed models
features.description: Amp chooses and routes models itself, so there is no model to pick in the profile.

features.title: API key sign-in
features.description: Add a key from your Amp settings. Amp may require paid credits.

features.title: Same workflow as other agents
features.description: Project chat, profiles, triggers and pull requests work the same way for Amp.

howItWorks.description: Paste an Amp API key in Settings → Agents.
Choose Amp in an agent profile.
SAM places the work on a machine and starts Amp in your devcontainer.

useCases.title: Teams already on Amp
useCases.description: Keep Amp as your agent while moving its sessions onto your own machines.

useCases.title: Comparing agents
useCases.description: Run Amp alongside Claude Code or Codex on the same project.

faq.question: Can I choose Amp's model?
faq.answer: No. Amp manages model selection itself.

faq.question: Does Amp support subscription sign-in in SAM?
faq.answer: No. SAM signs Amp in with an Amp API key.

faq.question: Where does Amp run?
faq.answer: On a cloud VM, inside your repository's devcontainer, using a cloud account connected to your SAM installation. A profile can choose an Instant session on Cloudflare Containers instead, which needs no cloud account but does not use your devcontainer.
